ai_agent_builder.title: Learn → Build → Run an AI agent
ai_agent_builder.summary: Move from agent concepts to a reproducible code workspace, model discovery, research compute, and model/API integration.

steps.purpose: Learn agent architecture, RAG, tool use, and research automation in a UCLA/QCBio setting.
steps.action: Review prerequisites and register for the workshop if the schedule fits.

steps.purpose: Unlock verified-student developer benefits and establish the GitHub identity used for the project.
steps.action: Verify student eligibility and activate the current benefits you actually need.

steps.purpose: Create a reproducible cloud development environment tied to the project repository.
steps.action: Open the repo in Codespaces or use an equivalent local environment.

steps.purpose: Discover candidate open models, datasets, model cards, licenses, and runnable examples.
steps.action: Shortlist models whose licenses and data requirements fit the project.

steps.purpose: Move the prototype to UCLA research cloud/GPU infrastructure when project scale or governance requires it.
steps.action: Check project eligibility, account setup, and approved data boundaries before provisioning compute.

steps.purpose: Compare multiple hosted model APIs behind a common interface for non-sensitive prototyping.
steps.action: Benchmark only approved test data and compare model behavior, latency, and cost.

single_cell_research.title: Learn → Reproduce → Scale a single-cell analysis
single_cell_research.summary: Start with UCLA single-cell training, establish a reproducible code environment, scale compute, then add literature and agentic support.

steps.purpose: Learn a practical UCLA single-cell RNA-seq workflow and analysis conventions.
steps.action: Review the workshop schedule, prerequisites, and materials.

steps.purpose: Set up the repository and student developer tooling used to make the workflow reproducible.
steps.action: Create or connect the analysis repository and keep data out of Git unless it is approved for sharing.

steps.purpose: Use a reproducible development container or cloud workspace for scripts and notebooks.
steps.action: Create the environment definition and run a small public/synthetic dataset first.

steps.purpose: Scale CPU/GPU work on UCLA-supported cloud infrastructure when local hardware is insufficient.
steps.action: Choose compute only after estimating memory, runtime, storage, and data-governance needs.

steps.purpose: Ground literature questions in the specific papers, protocols, and analysis notes you supply.
steps.action: Create a source notebook for methods, caveats, and interpretation support.

steps.purpose: Add bounded AI-agent automation around the deterministic analysis workflow.
steps.action: Automate routing/documentation tasks without delegating statistical validity to the agent.

coding_project.title: Set up → Code → Reproduce → Publish
coding_project.summary: Use student developer benefits, a development environment, AI coding assistance, and a reproducible cloud workspace to ship a public project.

steps.purpose: Verify student developer access and establish the GitHub project home.
steps.action: Activate only the benefits that support the project.

steps.purpose: Choose a professional IDE for coursework, academic research, or software development.
steps.action: Install the IDE that matches the project language and workflow.

steps.purpose: Add UCLA/GitHub AI pair-programming support when campus access is available.
steps.action: Verify current rollout status before depending on it.

steps.purpose: Make the environment reproducible in the browser/VS Code cloud workspace.
steps.action: Add a devcontainer or environment bootstrap so others can reproduce the app.

steps.purpose: Use UCLA-provided general AI for code explanation, debugging ideas, and documentation support.
steps.action: Keep source-of-truth logic in tests and code review rather than AI output.

gpu_compute.title: Prototype → Estimate → Scale compute
gpu_compute.summary: Start with a small notebook experiment, estimate requirements, then choose UCLA-supported or external GPU infrastructure.

steps.purpose: Prototype the workload in a hosted notebook with variable free compute.
steps.action: Measure memory, runtime, and accelerator needs on a small public/synthetic workload.

steps.purpose: Use UCLA research cloud/GPU infrastructure when project governance and scale make it the better fit.
steps.action: Confirm project/account eligibility and estimate cloud cost before scaling.

steps.purpose: Use code-defined external GPU execution for approved non-sensitive workloads or portable prototypes.
steps.action: Compare runtime and cost against BruinCloud before committing to a provider.

steps.purpose: Pair compute with model/dataset discovery and explicit model-card/license review.
steps.action: Select artifacts that fit the compute budget and license constraints.

literature_review.title: Collect → Ground → Synthesize → Automate
literature_review.summary: Ground questions in supplied sources first, then use general AI and optional APIs for structured, reproducible literature workflows.

steps.purpose: Create a source-grounded notebook from papers, URLs, protocols, and notes.
steps.action: Load only the sources you want the synthesis to rely on and inspect citations.

steps.purpose: Use UCLA-provided general AI for broader reasoning, drafting, and multimodal support.
steps.action: Separate source-grounded claims from broader web/model suggestions.

steps.purpose: Learn how LLM methods connect to genomics/research workflows in a QCBio setting.
steps.action: Use the workshop to improve evaluation and reproducibility practices.

steps.purpose: Programmatically scale structured literature tasks when an API workflow is justified.
steps.action: Use non-sensitive inputs, explicit schemas, and human review for uncertain classifications.

model_api_exploration.title: Compare → Benchmark → Integrate model APIs
model_api_exploration.summary: Use a gateway for breadth, then inspect direct providers and fast-inference options before selecting an integration path.

steps.purpose: Survey multiple hosted models and provider routes behind one API surface.
steps.action: Define a small benchmark set and record provider/model metadata with each result.

steps.purpose: Test low-latency hosted inference on supported models.
steps.action: Measure latency, output quality, and rate limits on the same benchmark.

steps.purpose: Benchmark direct OpenAI API access for the same task family.
steps.action: Record model/version, cost, and structured-output behavior.

steps.purpose: Benchmark direct Claude API access for reasoning, coding, and agentic tasks.
steps.action: Use the identical evaluation set and record failure modes.

steps.purpose: Benchmark Gemini developer APIs, including multimodal or long-context cases when relevant.
steps.action: Compare free/paid tier constraints and data terms before using research content.

steps.purpose: Re-evaluate the UCLA gateway as a campus-managed integration option when it becomes available.
steps.action: Check current UCLA availability before planning around this step.

cloud_learning.title: Student benefits → Cloud labs → Research cloud
cloud_learning.summary: Use verified-student programs for structured learning, then apply those skills to a real research cloud project.

steps.purpose: Establish verified student developer access and inspect current partner benefits.
steps.action: Verify eligibility and activate only the offers you need.

steps.purpose: Use structured Google Cloud labs and learning credits for cloud/AI skills.
steps.action: Treat learning credits as training credits, not a general production-compute grant.

steps.purpose: Learn AWS fundamentals and inspect the current learner labs/offers.
steps.action: Check the current portal rather than assuming a fixed promotional credit.

steps.purpose: Explore Azure with the current verified-student offer and its explicit credit window.
steps.action: Confirm eligibility, region, service limits, and expiry before provisioning resources.

steps.purpose: Apply cloud skills to UCLA research infrastructure when the project has a real compute need.
steps.action: Move from learning labs to governed research infrastructure only after scoping cost and data requirements.

general_ai.title: Discover → Learn → Build with UCLA AI
general_ai.summary: Start with UCLA-provided general AI, then move into campus training and a student developer workflow.

steps.purpose: Start with UCLA-provided general-purpose AI for reasoning, coding, and multimodal tasks.
steps.action: Try the task with non-sensitive content and learn the tool's strengths and limits.

steps.purpose: Compare another UCLA-provided general AI assistant and its web-grounded workflow.
steps.action: Use the same task so the comparison is concrete.

steps.purpose: Explore current UCLA AI training, demos, and student-focused sessions.
steps.action: Select the sessions most relevant to your next technical step.

steps.purpose: Turn learning into a real student software/research project with developer tooling.
steps.action: Create a small public or synthetic project and document what you learned.
